analysis.file_name: Merck & Co. (MRK)_ Second Global Ph3 Data for Sac-TMT Provides Continued Validation for Significant Pipeline Asset.pdf
analysis.title: Merck & Co. (MRK): Second Global Ph3 Data for Sac-TMT Provides Continued Validation for Significant Pipeline Asset
key_insights: MRK announced that TroFuse-015, the global Ph3 trial of sac-TMT in 3L+ advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, met its primary endpoint of improved overall survival (OS).
The secondary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) was not met. GS views this as less relevant given positive OS and notes oncology precedents where OS was achieved without PFS.
This is the second positive global Ph3 for sac-TMT, after TroFuse-005 in endometrial cancer. GS calls it continued global validation, building on partner Kelun's data at ESMO.

The indication is a relatively small part of the sac-TMT program: GS models $81mn unadjusted 2035 sales at 55% probability of success, or $44mn risk-adjusted, against $7,108mn risk-adjusted for the whole program.
GS sees sac-TMT as a key candidate to replace the revenue gap from Keytruda's upcoming patent expiration.
MRK will present the data at an upcoming medical meeting (GS flags ASCO-GU in January) and share it with regulators.
No Kelun Ph3 trial exists in this indication. In Kelun's Ph1/2 SKB264-01 gastric/GEJ cohort (50% in 3L+), sac-TMT monotherapy showed mPFS 3.7 months and mOS 7.6 months in the 3L+ subgroup.
Further sac-TMT trials in larger indications read out starting in 2027, and MRK will start Ph3 combination studies with its PD-1xVEGF bispecific in 1H27.

MRK shares sold off this week on broader pressure on Pharma stocks and MRK-specific underperformance. GS says investors see no near-term catalyst into year-end, and views the pullback as an entry point into 2027.
MRK shares are below their level before the initial positive intismeran (Moderna-partnered) adjuvant melanoma data. GS sees this as an over-correction.
GS rates MRK Buy with a $165 12m PT, based on 17.0x P/E on Q5-Q8 adjusted EPS, implying 24.2% upside from $132.81.

market_movers.rationale: Positive OS in the second global sac-TMT Ph3 supports the pipeline thesis for replacing Keytruda revenue. GS sees the recent selloff as an entry point.

sector_views.rationale: The report gives no sector stance. It notes that broader market dynamics weighed on Pharma stocks this week.

earnings_insights: GS estimates MRK EPS of $2.80 for 12/26E, $8.50 for 12/27E and $10.20 for 12/28E, against $8.98 reported for 12/25. These are GS estimates, not reported figures.
GS quarterly EPS: $(0.13) for 6/26 and estimates of $2.49 for 9/26E, $1.72 for 12/26E and $2.07 for 3/27E.
GS revenue estimates: $67,338mn for 12/26E, $68,434mn for 12/27E and $72,494mn for 12/28E, against $65,011mn for 12/25.
risk_factors: Faster-than-expected erosion of Keytruda after loss of exclusivity, or lower-than-expected conversion to subcutaneous Keytruda.
Further slowdown in established vaccine products and a slower ramp of newly launched products.
Regulatory uncertainty, and a tougher regulatory and market environment for vaccines, the FDA, tariffs and M&A.
vol_and_positioning: Investors see no near-term or imminent catalyst for MRK into year-end, per GS conversations. MRK has underperformed peers this week.
